prompts.name: map_from_image
prompts.title: Draw a map from a picture
prompts.description: Recreate a reference picture (screenshot, render or hand sketch) as a tile map with the user's tilesets and stamps.

arguments.name: reference
arguments.description: Absolute path of the picture (.png/.jpg/.webp), or a referenceId from get_session.references.

arguments.name: map
arguments.description: Map name or id to draw on (default: the active map).

prompts.template:
Recreate the picture {{reference}} as a tile map on {{map}} in Harita. Use only Harita tools (no shell, Python or files). Do not trace the picture by eye: alignment, quantizer and object search are cell-exact.

1. get_session: map id, layers, smart sources (smart) and references. If {{reference}} is a file path, call reference_add {path}; if it is already in references, use its referenceId. If the tile pack ships a sample .tmx/.tmj of this picture, import_tiled {path} instead and stop at step 7.
2. reference_align {referenceId, mapId}: check the grid in its preview (lines on tile seams); if wrong, call again with hint {scale, offsetX, offsetY}. Look at the art: get_tile_catalog for each tileset, list_stamps {includeSheet:true}.
3. begin_edit {mapIds:[mapId], requestLabel}. Keep transactionId and resumeToken. After reconnect: resume_edit with your resumeToken (or pass resumeToken on the next write).
4. reference_quantize {referenceId, mapId} (ground + transparent overlay layers, light-normalized), then paint_grid {proposalId} (do not retype the rows). Flat-colour sketch: mode:"sketch" with colorLegend (each colour → {random:[main tile weight 8, 1–2 similar weight 1–2]}, a tile or {stampId}); redraw its rivers/roads with draw_path (smart source) and ponds with smart_brush mode area.
5. reference_detect_objects {referenceId, mapId}: place_stamp each positionsByStamp entry (positions), each flipped[] entry (with its flipX/flipY), then each stacked[] entry (with its layerMapping, so the object behind keeps its cells). Objects with no stamp: suggest_stamps on the tileset, show the candidates to the user and create_stamp only the ones they accept, then detect again.
6. render_compare {referenceId, mapId, cells:true}: fix its worst cells (use their alternatives) with paint_grid / replace_tiles / clear_region; repeat until stats.pctBelow.deltaE5 stops improving.
7. validate_map (read hints), finish_edit {summary}, and tell the user the draft waits for Onayla.

prompts.name: map_from_text
prompts.title: Draw a map from a description
prompts.description: Design a tile map from a text description with the user's tilesets and stamps.

arguments.name: description
arguments.description: What to draw, e.g. 'a village with a river, a bridge, a road and five houses'.

arguments.name: map
arguments.description: Map name or id to draw on (default: the active map).

prompts.template:
Draw this on {{map}} in Harita: {{description}}
Use only Harita tools (no shell, Python or files). Aim for a hand-made level, not a diagram.

1. get_session: map id, layers, smart sources (smart). get_tile_catalog for each tileset and list_stamps {includeSheet:true} to see the art and stamp sizes.
2. Plan in map cells (x right, y down): water and main roads first, then a cluster of buildings along the road, fields/gardens, tree clumps (3–8 trees) and a forest band along 1–2 edges. Keep paths connected and leave at least 1 free cell around every house.
3. begin_edit {mapIds:[mapId], requestLabel}. Keep transactionId and resumeToken. After reconnect: resume_edit with your resumeToken (or pass resumeToken on the next write).
4. Ground: one paint_rect over the whole map with value {random:[main grass weight 8, 1–2 similar variants weight 1–2]}.
5. Water and roads: draw_path with a smart source (points at the bends; width 3 for a river, 2 for a main road), ponds with smart_brush mode area. Draw a road that crosses water straight across in one draw_path, then place the bridge stamp over the crossing, covering the full water width.
6. Buildings, trees and fences: place_stamp (positions for many copies). Give every door a 1-wide draw_path to the road that ends on the cell just below the door (never into or under a stamp); fences as closed outlines around a field or garden; trees in clumps and edge forest, never evenly spread single trees.
7. Details on the upper layer: bushes, flowers, rocks with paint_cells points near paths and houses, so no large area stays empty.
8. render_preview {grid:true, coordinates:true}; zoom into joins; fix with paint_grid / replace_tiles / clear_region.
9. validate_map (fix every hint, e.g. PATH_UNDER_STAMP), finish_edit {summary}, and tell the user the draft waits for Onayla.
